subject: Dedicated capacity: parity request, preemption protection & smoothing concession
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medicai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@medicai.com>; procurement@medicai.com
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity ask and parity request for Q3 commit

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We ran the numbers internally and have a firm Q3 committed need: 48 reserved GPUs for a 12-month term. Our engineering lead is pushing for H200 class for latency-critical inference, but we understand availability constraints.

If Redwood can provide either: (A) guaranteed H200 parity for peak windows or (B) a formal H100 -> H200 parity plan that includes preemption protection and a capping mechanism on overage rates, we'll sign the commitment this week.

Specific asks from our procurement side (Samantha copied):
- A 72-hour reservation hold for planned deployment windows (to avoid losing capacity during go-live).
- A capped overage rate that prevents surprise billing during ramp (proposal: $6.00 / GPU-hour cap).
- A temporary smoothing credit for month 1 (to offset warm-up spikiness).

We've attached our rolling plan and the mutual action plan. Can you advise whether Deal Desk / Execs would consider a one-time onboarding concession or a short-term preemption SLA for the first quarter? We can be flexible on exact discounting if terms are protective.

Best,
Tom
Tom Ellis
VP Product, MedicAI

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:09:00 -0700
Subject: EXEC APPROVAL REQUEST: MedicAI dedicated capacity concessions (deal MED-2027-0791)

Hi Lauren / Karthik —

Summary: MedicAI (48 GPU reserved commit, 12 months) is asking for non-standard capacity assurances to meet a firm go-live in early August. They prefer H200 but will accept H100 if we provide specific protections. Procurement needs an answer within 48 hours to keep the PO timeline on track.

I recommend we approve a controlled concession set to convert this into a predictable, low-risk deal:

Proposal (Deal Desk recommended, requires Exec sign-off):
- One-time onboarding credit: 15% credit applied to month-1 reserved invoice (to offset warm-up spikes).
- Preemption protection for scheduled windows: provide a written 72-hour reservation hold for up to three planned go-live windows during the first quarter after start date (no additional recurring fee).
- Overage smoothing: cap overage rate at $6.00 / GPU-hour for first 60 days after activation. After 60 days, standard overage rates apply.
- Operational note: reservation holds will be honored by not reallocating the reserved capacity for the protected window; Aditya notes we need to provision buffer capacity 48 hours prior to the window to avoid contention.

Rationale: This addresses customer risk aversion without a long-term price concession. The 15% onboarding credit is limited to month-1 only and reduces friction to sign. Forecasted P&L impact: estimated ~2.2% reduction in first-quarter ARR for this deal vs list pricing, with high probability of renewal given their growth trajectory.

If you approve, I'll send a concise amendment and the explicit service note to MedicAI and instruct Billing to apply the credit on the first invoice. If you want an alternate concession (e.g., a smaller credit + extended cap duration), say so and I'll rework the wording.

Approve options (reply with one of the following):
- APPROVE as written
- APPROVE with reduced credit (10%)
- DECLINE (we keep standard terms)

Thanks for a quick turnaround — procurement needs to know by EOD Monday.

Hannah
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
